name: Lever-Colossus
description: Lever-Colossus is among the largest gas giants in the surveyed volume, a world so massive that its gravitational influence extends like a lever across the entire system, tilting the orbits of neighboring planets and capturing passing comets into a vast retinue of irregular moons. The atmosphere is a deep, brooding crimson banded with streaks of gold, its cloud layers extending for thousands of kilometers in depth. A colossal storm system at the equator has been raging for longer than human civilization has existed in the sector, its eye a dark vortex that swallows all light.

The sheer scale of Lever-Colossus creates psychological effects that go beyond the physical. Pilots report a sense of vertigo when approaching, the planet filling their viewports until the curvature of the horizon becomes imperceptible and the cloud surface appears as an infinite, heaving plain. The gravity near the cloud tops is crushing, the radiation environment lethal, and the magnetic storms unpredictable, creating a triple threat that has earned the planet its reputation as the most dangerous refueling stop in the sector.

Localized gravity wells have been detected at multiple points in the upper atmosphere, regions where the gravitational field spikes to values inconsistent with the planet's known mass distribution. These anomalies move through the atmosphere on their own trajectories, sometimes clustering together, sometimes dispersing across hemispheres, in patterns that some analysts insist show signs of intentional movement. Whether they represent exotic matter concentrations, atmospheric density fluctuations, or something else entirely remains unknown.

Lever-Colossus's helium-3 reserves are effectively infinite, but the mortality rate among skimming operations is the highest in the sector. The moving gravity wells add an element of unpredictability that no amount of preparation can fully mitigate, as their sudden appearance near a skimming vessel can crush it into the deeper atmosphere. Military and commercial interests continue to send crews because the fuel is too valuable to forgo, but every pilot who makes the approach does so knowing that Lever-Colossus takes a toll, and the toll is paid in ships and lives.
